10.0.s.en: (1) The mission of the seventy apostles

10.0.0.en: Others, that is, other than the twelve disciples, and each of them is considered an apostle and a general bishop in the service afterward for the whole world; but the seventy apostles did not receive any priestly rank, though some of them became deacons like the seven deacons mentioned in (Acts 6:3), and some of them were appointed by the Twelve as priests or bishops to help them in the service.

10.0.1.en: Christ chose seventy men from the crowds who followed Him, in whom He saw love for Him and for the service. St. Ambrose says that they were 72) (but St. Luke wrote the approximate number, that is, 70), (but the Church mentions them in her prayers by their full number, which is 72).(Christ had previously sent the twelve disciples, and then sent the seventy apostles.

10.0.2.en: The number twelve points to the twelve tribes of Israel, while the seventy apostles point to the seventy elders whom Moses chose to judge the people (Num 11:16-25).

10.0.3.en: In view of the breadth of the ministry that Christ would carry out and the shortness of the time, He sent them to the cities and villages in which He would preach, to prepare souls to hear His teachings, and He sent them two by two so that each might encourage the other. St. Luke alone mentions the seventy apostles and their mission, because they were sent to towns in the region of Perea, which is east of the Jordan, where the Jews were mixed with the Gentiles; for the Gospel of Luke was written to the Gentiles and so is concerned with their ministry.

10.1.0.en: Christ declares a permanent truth, which is the multitude of souls needing the proclamation compared with the number of servants, and He sets down the solution, which is prayer, that God may choose servants for Himself and stir their feelings to love Him and serve Him. It is good that you begin your service with prayer, relying on God in it and on His support by sending servants who will complete the work with you and after you.

10.2.0.en: The service seems difficult when the lamb is to preach to the wolf, but the power of God with the lamb makes it change fierce souls like the wolf into gentle souls like the lamb, so it supports the lamb and protects it from the attacks and persecutions of the wicked. And if God permits the servant to suffer or even die for His sake, He will give him a great place in heaven and use his endurance of sufferings to rebuke the wicked and bring them back to Him by repentance so that they believe and are saved. Do not meet evil with evil, because violence is a disturbance within a person. So be calm, relying on your mighty Christ, to absorb the rage of the violent and declare your strong love for the wicked, for even if they despise it at first, it will affect them afterward ... and so you keep your calm and win others.

10.3.0.en: A purse: in which they carried their gold, their silver and all their money.

10.3.1.en: A scrip: in which they carry their food.

10.3.2.en: Shoes: because they would not endure the much walking between the cities and villages during the preaching, so they rely on God, who provides for all their needs.

10.3.3.en: Salute no man: one must concentrate on the aim, which is preaching, so that no one is occupied with many greetings, and of course what is meant is not that they should not show a greeting to those they meet.

10.3.4.en: Christ stresses the necessity of relying on Him and not on material things.

10.4.0.en: The son of peace: the one who welcomes peace and is worthy of it.

10.4.1.en: Your peace shall rest upon it: he enjoys the good news of salvation, and so receives peace in his life.

10.4.2.en: It shall turn to you again: you keep the grace of peace and of the salvation that is in Christ, and it abides in you.

10.4.3.en: He commands them to offer peace and love to everyone they meet, and if anyone refuses, they are not to be disturbed, because those who refuse lose the peace offered to them, and God establishes peace in the hearts of the servants so that they may continue their service of bringing peace to all.

10.5.0.en: Christ encourages His apostles to take their necessary needs from those to whom they preach, namely food, drink and a place to stay, the fewest necessities. And they are to eat whatever is set before them, not refusing the foods of the Gentiles which may be forbidden to the Jews, because this prohibition was a symbol of rejecting sins, not because of any evil in this food, and so that they would not cause the Gentiles to whom they preach to stumble.

10.5.1.en: The labourer is worthy of his hire: the servant deserves to receive his necessary needs from the service, and not be occupied with providing them, so as to concentrate all his effort on the service and the preaching.

10.5.2.en: And He commands them not to move from house to house seeking a better place or food, but to stay in one place, concentrating on their aim, which is the service.

10.5.3.en: Eat such things as are set before you: be content with the food set before you, and do not ask for other kinds.

10.6.0.en: The aim of the preaching is to alert people to the nearness of the Kingdom of God, that is, to prepare for it by repentance and a holy life, and He supported them by the working of miracles of healing to confirm their message and to draw souls to hear their teaching.

10.7.0.en: Go your ways out into the streets of the same: proclaim to all the crowds of the city.

10.7.1.en: Even the very dust of your city, which cleaveth on us, we do wipe off against you: that is, we took nothing from you, not even the dust, for we seek no material gain.

10.7.2.en: Be sure of this: a specific and clear warning that they may repent.

10.7.3.en: The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you: Christ wants to reign over your hearts, so do not persist in rejecting Him, because the end of your life is near and you will face God the Judge.

10.8.0.en: The city of Sodom was famous for evil and God burned it (Gen 19). And the cities of Tyre and Sidon, God commanded the destruction of both for their evils in ancient times (Isa 23), but the cities that reject the teachings of Christ and His apostles, like Capernaum (whose people were characterized by pride and refused to believe in Christ, who had done among them many miracles and many teachings), and like Chorazin and Bethsaida, their punishment in the judgment will be heavier than that of the cities destroyed in ancient times.

10.8.1.en: Because whoever knows more is asked to give more, whoever enjoyed the ministry of the New Testament and refused will have a greater punishment than one who refused God's teachings in the Old Testament, because the teachings of the New Testament are clearer and more powerful.

10.9.0.en: Christ made clear that the apostles represent Him, so His teachings are on their lips, and whoever receives the teachings of the apostles has received Christ Himself, and whoever despises their teachings has despised Christ, and consequently despises God the Father who sent Him.

10.9.1.en: Do not reject the voice of God in every counsel you hear, not only in the Church, the Holy Bible and the father of confession, but pay attention also to the counsels of those around you.

10.10.s.en: (2) The results of the apostles' mission

10.10.0.en: The apostles rejoiced at the success of their mission and at people's acceptance of their preaching, and perhaps they had healed many sick, but what drew their attention was the submission of the demons to them when they commanded them to come out of the people tormented by them.

10.11.0.en: Christ confirmed His apostles' joy by declaring that He had seen Satan fall like lightning from heaven, that is, the beginning of the shattering of his authority, which would be completed by the Cross, since he was shaken as a result of their preaching and the casting out of his helpers the demons from many souls, and the beginning of people's return to God by repentance.

10.12.0.en: Christ gave His apostles authority, not only over the demons, but over all their works and their stirring up of creation against human beings. In ancient times he moved the serpent in Paradise and brought down Adam and Eve, and he still stirs up animals like serpents and scorpions to harm man, and even stirs up trials and troubles to harm them, but all this has come under the authority of the apostles to prevent it by the power of God, as appeared in the lives of the saints and the children of God throughout history.

10.13.0.en: Christ directed their sight to the more important joy, which is their being counted children of the Kingdom, by their spiritual conduct in faith, repentance and striving in every virtue. This is far greater than great gifts such as casting out demons or healing the sick, because a gift does not justify its possessor if he does not repent and live with God, whereas the fruits of the Holy Spirit and the virtuous life guarantee the Kingdom of Heaven. And if the names have been written, they must be kept and made firm by continuing in spiritual conduct until death so that they may not be blotted out.

10.13.1.en: Do not be occupied with gifts such as the ability to preach and teach, but rather live with God in repentance and love, for this is what guarantees your salvation. And if you are given a gift, use it to glorify God with humility lest you fall like the proud Satan.

10.13.2.en: Carry your cross in endurance and labor, and the lusts of the world and its fears will not harm you.

10.14.0.en: Christ offered a prayer to the Father, which is a conversation within the divine Being, just as a person speaks to himself in a dialogue within his mind.

10.14.1.en: This prayer was joy, exultation and thanksgiving for the grace that overflowed upon weak human beings who are humble like children, that is, the disciples and apostles, and they preached the Kingdom of God. At the same time this wisdom was hidden from the proud who are wise in their own eyes, like the scribes and Pharisees and the philosophers of the world. For God, the Creator and Ruler of all, rejoices to give His grace to the humble that they may become the wisest on earth.

10.14.2.en: To the extent that you humble yourself before God and people, God gives you wisdom, so that you know the way of your salvation, discern between matters and draw many to faith.

10.15.0.en: Here He declares the equality of the Son with the Father, for He has all the authority of the Father, and no one knows the essence of the Son but the Father, nor the essence of the Father but the Son, and then the Son gives His knowledge to the humble who love Him.

10.16.0.en: Christ praised His disciples by blessing them (how happy they are), because they saw Him and believed His good news, which the prophets and righteous kings of the Old Testament, such as David, longed to see, namely the Christ of whom they prophesied. Thank God every day that you were born a Christian and enjoy the Holy Sacraments; eternal happiness awaits you after the striving of this life.

10.17.0.en: The lawyer is one of the scholars of the Law, a class of the scribes distinguished by their deep study of the Mosaic Law, and he came to tempt Christ and to catch Him in an error, so his question was ill-intentioned and not of pure purpose. He asked Him about the way to reach the eternal Kingdom, hoping that Christ would point to other ways than the commandments and the Law, and so would be against Moses and the Old Testament. The lawyer's conversation with Christ is different from the ruler's question to Him mentioned in (ch. 18:18-30), though there is some similarity in their question about eternity.

10.18.0.en: Christ knew that the lawyer meant to tempt Him, so He answered his question with another question, namely, What is written in the law? how readest thou? that is, what is the summary of the commandments and the Law?

10.19.0.en: The lawyer's answer showed his knowledge of the Ten Commandments, and he summarized them in two commandments, the love of God and the love of one's neighbor, as mentioned in (Deut 6:5; Lev 19:18).

10.20.0.en: Christ praised the lawyer's answer although He knew that he was tempting Him, and told him to carry out what he had summarized, that is, this love, in order to inherit eternal life.

10.20.1.en: It is good to know much about spiritual things, but the more important thing is to apply them in your life in order to be with Christ.

10.21.s.en: (5) The parable of the good Samaritan

10.21.0.en: Since the lawyer could not find a fault in Christ's words, he asked Him another question on which opinions differ, namely, who is the neighbor: is he the Jew only, or can others be added, or is it limited to some Jews and not all?

10.22.0.en: Christ answered the lawyer with a parable, which is the story of a Jewish man who was in Jerusalem, which stands on a mountain, and was traveling to the city of Jericho, which lies lower than Jerusalem by about 1000 meters (a thousand meters), and is seven hours distant from it by a stony road with no cultivation, full of caves and therefore much frequented by robbers, and called the Red Way because of the much bloodshed in it.

10.22.1.en: Robbers attacked this traveler and stole what he had, even his clothes, and beat him and wounded him, and left him in a bad condition near to death.

10.22.2.en: This man points to mankind, and Jerusalem is the place of peace and life with God, and Jericho, the city with low walls, represents the world and its lusts, while the robbers are the demons who fight human beings with sins, and steal from them the garments of righteousness, and wound them with iniquities, and leave them in a state of spiritual weakness near to death, because they left Jerusalem, that is, the Church, and went down to the occupations of the world .. that is, Jericho.

10.23.0.en: He saw him from afar: although his condition called for drawing near to him and helping him, he did not care and was content to look from far away and then left him.

10.23.1.en: The priest is a symbol of the Law and the statutes, which were unable to deliver mankind from its sins, but looked and judged it only with weakness.

10.23.2.en: One of the priests going down from Jerusalem to Jericho passed by this traveler, and stood and looked and saw his bad condition, but it seems that he feared to help him lest the robbers attack him, or because of his preoccupation with his own affairs, he left him and did not help him.

10.24.0.en: A Levite: the tribe of Levi was consecrated to the service of the Temple, and each member of it is a servant like the deacon or the servant in the New Testament.

10.24.1.en: Came and looked: he drew near him and saw his hard condition, which needed quick relief, but because of the hardness of his heart he did not care and left him and went on.

10.24.2.en: A Levite passed by going down from Jerusalem, and looked and saw this traveler, but he did not help him and left him and went on, probably for the same reasons that the priest thought of.

10.24.3.en: The Levite is a symbol of the prophets in the Old Testament, who declared the word of God to mankind but could not deliver it from the sentence of death passed upon it.

10.25.0.en: A Samaritan: one of the inhabitants of the northern part of the land of the Jews, who are Jews that separated from the worship in Jerusalem and worshipped idols, so a boycott arose between them and the Jews, and a Samaritan does not mingle with any Jew. After that a Samaritan man came, and passed along this road and saw the wounded man and his bad condition, and feelings of tenderness and compassion were stirred toward him.

10.25.1.en: The word Samaritan means keeper, and he is a symbol of Christ, full of tenderness, who had compassion on fallen mankind, and redeemed it with His blood and guarded it from the wars of the demons.

10.26.0.en: He set him on his own beast, which bore the toil of walking along the road, to give rest to the wounded man riding on the beast, and even supported him all along the way until he reached the inn.

10.26.1.en: The Samaritan drew near to the wounded man and gave him relief, for he bound up his wounds with pieces of his clothes after pouring oil and wine on them, which were the materials used for relieving wounds at that time, and then carried him on his beast and stayed beside him until he brought him to an inn, and took care of his food, drink and rest.

10.26.2.en: Christ covered our sins and treated them with His righteousness, and put on them oil, to soften the wound, and wine to cleanse it, the first soothing and the second painful; so the Holy Spirit treats our sins with gentleness and firmness. Then He set him on the beast, which represents the Body of Christ in which He bore all our sins and toils, and brought him to the inn, that is, the Church, where he finds all care and rest and food, which is His most holy Body and Blood.

10.27.0.en: After the Samaritan had watched over the wounded man's rest, he charged the innkeeper to take care of him and gave him two pence (enough to feed 50 persons one meal at that time), and promised to come after a while to visit him, and if he spent more than the two pence, he would give him all that he had spent.

10.27.1.en: After Christ accomplished redemption and rose from the dead, He charged His disciples, that is, the bishops of the Church, to take care of mankind, and gave them two pence, which point to the knowledge of the Father and the Son, or to love, because love is between two, or to the Holy Bible with its two Testaments, that is, the word of God, and then He promised to come at His second coming and recompense His Church and His servants for all their labor, however much they have spent.

10.28.0.en: After relating this parable to him, Christ asked the lawyer, Which of these three, who passed by this traveler, was neighbor to him?

10.29.0.en: The lawyer was compelled to declare the truth, which is that the Samaritan is the nearest person to this wounded Jew, though he did not mention the name of the Samaritan, but said, He that shewed mercy on him, because the Jews hate the Samaritans. Christ answered him that he should live by this love, and so be a neighbor to every person in the world. By this Christ changed the Jews' concept of kinship and love, so that in Christianity the heart is enlarged to love all, however far off or rejected they may be.

10.29.1.en: Do not neglect the needs of one who asks your help, and hasten to his aid before your preoccupations make you forget to attend to the work of mercy. And if he does not ask your help out of shyness, do not be slack toward him, but seek out the needy of every kind, especially the spiritually needy, that is, those far from God, to help them.

10.30.0.en: As they went: on the way of their journey toward Jerusalem.

10.30.1.en: A certain village: it is Bethany, and it is about three quarters of an hour from Jerusalem.

10.30.2.en: Christ was accustomed to go to the village of Bethany and rest in the house of Lazarus and his two sisters Martha and Mary, and it seems that Martha had precedence in leading and caring for guests, so she received Christ into their house.

10.31.0.en: Martha took care to prepare a splendid feast worthy of her great guest, the Lord Jesus, and Mary shared with her in the beginning, but when Christ began His life-giving teachings Mary felt that it was better to be content with some foods, and she took care to sit near Christ at His feet in humility to enjoy His teachings.

10.32.0.en: Hath left me: this means that Mary was helping Martha to prepare the food at first, and then left her because she felt that listening to Christ's words was more important than many dishes at the feast, and it was better to be content with what had been prepared first.

10.32.1.en: Martha continued preparing the splendid feast, and was not convinced by Mary's view. From the amount of work her nerves became strained, and she fell into condemnation of Christ and of her sister Mary, accusing Him of indifference to her many labors and of failing to tell Mary to share with her in preparing the great feast, and she asked Him to command her sister to leave listening to His teachings and help her.

10.33.0.en: Despite the importance of what Martha was doing, which is preparing the food necessary for bodily life, she was absorbed in it to an exaggerated degree, to the point that she became troubled, so Christ reproved her. He of course appreciates her love and her care to honor Him, but excessive preoccupation with honoring Christ materially can confuse a person and strain him.

10.34.0.en: One thing is needful: that is, attachment to Christ and learning from Him, and not excessive care for the needs of the body.

10.34.1.en: Christ made clear that one dish, or the necessary food, is enough. On the other hand, Mary chose the good part, which is hearing His teachings, over being absorbed in material works, and this choice is what satisfies the soul and saves it forever.

10.34.2.en: Shall not be taken away: for the love of Christ endures in the heart and brings the Christian to the eternal Kingdom, and does not perish like foods and material things.

10.34.3.en: Martha is a symbol of material services and useful human works in all fields of life, while Mary is a symbol of the love of the word of God and meditation on it, and this is the more important, and the soul is not saved without it. For although Christ appreciates useful worldly works and all material services, such as helping the sick and the elderly and supporting the poor materially, yet they do not exempt the servant or the spiritual person from his personal relationship with Christ in the Church through the Holy Sacraments, prayer, reading the Holy Bible and spiritual sermons.

10.34.4.en: Do not be absorbed in material works, even if they are service for Christ, to the neglect of the worship of God, and give priority to your prayers, your readings and your enjoyment of the Holy Sacraments. And even in service, learn and apply the spiritual meanings in your own life before you tell them to others.

10.34.5.en: Prayer and overcoming the demons. The Lord's Prayer (vv. 1-4):

10.34.6.en: The Lord's Prayer is mentioned in (Mt 6:9-15), and it is noted that Luke is not concerned with order, since it was said before this time that Luke mentions.

10.34.7.en: 1- And it came to pass, that, as he was praying in a certain place, when he ceased, one of his disciples said unto him, "Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples." 2- And he said unto them, "When ye pray, say, Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth. 3- Give us day by day our daily bread. 4- And forgive us our sins; for we also forgive every one that is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation; but deliver us from evil."
